facts.activity_series: maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment

control_failures.control_label: secondary containment by bund and drainage
integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: near hit - chemical exposure at LA-7202

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the integrity of the mechanical seal support system on LA-7202 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically monitoring seal-face condition and temperature. LA-7202 (marine loading arms) is in service for ship loading. The task proceeded during an intrusive maintenance task while the secondary containment by bund and drainage was in place but did not perform. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 12 April 2007 a near hit was recorded on LA-7202 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during an intrusive maintenance task; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
